paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of novel treatments for patients suffering from serious hematologic diseases. We have assembled a portfolio of clinical and preclinical product candidates that aim to modify fundamental biological pathways associated with the formation and function of red blood cells, specifically heme biosynthesis and iron homeostasis. Our current pipeline includes bitopertin for the treatment of erythropoietic porphyrias, or EPs, including erythropoietic protoporphyria, or EPP, and X-linked protoporphyria, or XLP; DISC-0974 for the treatment of anemia of myelofibrosis, or MF, and anemia of inflammatory bowel disease, or IBD; and DISC-3405 for the treatment of polycythemia vera, or PV, sickle cell disease, or SCD, and other hematologic disorders. In addition, our preclinical programs include DISC-0998 for the treatment of anemia associated with inflammatory diseases. Our approach to product candidate development leverages well-understood molecular mechanisms that have been validated in humans. We believe that each of our product candidates, if approved, has the potential to improve the lives of patients suffering from hematologic diseases.

Bitopertin is the lead product candidate in our heme biosynthesis modulation portfolio. Bitopertin was previously evaluated by F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd and Hoffmann-La Roche Inc., or collectively, Roche, in a comprehensive clinical program in over 4,000 individuals in other indications which demonstrated the activity of bitopertin as a glycine transporter 1, or GlyT1, inhibitor and its effect on heme biosynthesis. We are initially developing bitopertin for the treatment of EPs, including EPP and XLP, which are part of a group of severe diseases, known as porphyrias, caused by defects in the heme biosynthesis pathway that cause an accumulation of toxic metabolites referred to as porphyrins, resulting in skin hypersensitivity to sunlight and some types of artificial light.

We have completed two Phase 2 clinical trials of bitopertin: BEACON, an open-label, parallel-dose clinical trial in EPP and XLP patients conducted at sites in Australia, and AURORA, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial in EPP patients conducted at sites in the United States. In both trials, bitopertin significantly reduced the toxic metabolite, protoporphyrin IX, or PPIX, and was associated with improvements in measures of time spent in sunlight and quality of life. In addition, bitopertin was generally well-tolerated. All participants in AURORA and BEACON were eligible to participate in HELIOS, an ongoing open-label, long-term extension study of bitopertin in EPP and XLP patients. Interim data from HELIOS, presented in June 2025, demonstrated that longer term treatment of bitopertin was associated with sustained reductions in PPIX, as well as improvements in quality of life and liver biomarkers. In our end-of-Phase 2 meeting in September 2024, the U.S. Food & Drug Administration, or the FDA, agreed with the potential for reduction of PPIX to serve as a surrogate endpoint to support a potential accelerated approval of bitopertin in EPP and XLP. In our Type C meeting in December 2024, we aligned with the FDA on the design of APOLLO, a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial of bitopertin in EPP and XLP patients that in the setting of an accelerated approval would serve as a post-marketing confirmatory trial. We initiated the APOLLO trial in May 2025 and in September 2025 we submitted a New Drug Application, or NDA, for accelerated approval of bitopertin in EPP and XLP in the United States based on our existing data. In October 2025, we were awarded a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher, or CNPV, from the FDA for bitopertin in EPP and XLP. The CNPV program, announced in June 2025, is designed to accelerate the development and review of certain drugs aligned with US national health priorities. The FDA accepted our NDA for review in November 2025 and in February 2026 issued a complete response letter, or CRL. Although the FDA agreed that clinical data from AURORA and BEACON provided sufficient evidence that bitopertin significantly lowers whole blood metal-free PPIX, the FDA concluded that the trials did not show evidence of association between percent change in PPIX and sunlight exposure-based endpoints as measured in the trials. As such, the FDA determined that there is uncertainty regarding whether bitopertin's effect on PPIX is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, despite the strong mechanistic and biological plausibility supporting the use of the PPIX biomarker in protoporphyria. The FDA indicated that results of the ongoing APOLLO trial could serve as evidence to support a potential traditional approval, and we plan to request a Type A meeting to review our approach with the FDA. We expect to report topline data from APOLLO in the fourth quarter of 2026, following which we plan to submit a response to the CRL.

Our APOLLO clinical trial is also intended to serve as a registrational trial with respect to any potential future marketing applications for bitopertin in EPP and XLP outside the United States. We continue to evaluate potential additional trials of bitopertin in other indications.

DISC-0974 is the lead product candidate in our iron homeostasis portfolio and was licensed from AbbVie Deutschland GmbH & Co. KG, or AbbVie. DISC-0974 is designed to suppress hepcidin production and increase serum iron levels. We completed a Phase 1 clinical trial in healthy volunteers in the United States in June 2022, with results showing an acceptable tolerability profile and evidence of target engagement, iron mobilization and augmented erythropoiesis. We initiated a Phase 1b/2 clinical trial in June 2022 in patients with anemia of MF, with results from the Phase 1b portion of this clinical trial showing substantial and sustained reductions in hepcidin levels and increases in iron alongside strong hematologic responses across patient types and an acceptable tolerability profile. We initiated RALLY-MF, the open-label Phase 2 portion of this clinical trial, in December 2024 and reported initial data from this Phase 2 trial in December 2025, with results demonstrating meaningful overall anemia responses across all patient subgroups, regardless of baseline transfusion status and independent of concomitant Janus Kinase, or JAK, inhibitor therapy use. Topline data from this trial is expected in the second half of 2026, which, if positive, is expected to support discussions with regulatory agencies on the potential regulatory path for DISC-0974 in anemia of MF. We initiated a Phase 2 clinical trial of DISC-0974 in patients with IBD and anemia in the first quarter of 2026, and we are planning exploratory studies in additional patient populations with anemia of chronic disease. We are also developing a preclinical anti-hemojuvelin, or HJV, monoclonal antibody, DISC-0998, which also targets hepcidin suppression and was licensed from AbbVie. DISC-0998 is designed to increase serum iron levels and has an extended serum half-life as compared to DISC-0974. We believe this profile may be desirable in certain subsets of patients with anemia associated with inflammatory diseases.

In addition, we are developing DISC-3405, a monoclonal antibody against Transmembrane Serine Protease 6, or TMPRSS6, that we licensed from Mabwell Therapeutics, Inc., or Mabwell. DISC-3405 is part of our iron homeostasis portfolio and is designed to induce hepcidin production and reduce serum iron levels. We initiated a Phase 1 clinical trial of DISC-3405 in healthy adult volunteers in October 2023 and presented interim data from the single-ascending dose, or SAD, portion of this clinical trial in June 2024. We presented data from the multiple ascending dose, or MAD, portion of this clinical trial in December 2024, and presented updated data from both the SAD and MAD portions of this clinical trial in June 2025, with results showing an acceptable tolerability profile and evidence of target engagement, including dose-related increases in serum hepcidin and corresponding reductions in serum iron across all dose levels. We are developing DISC-3405 for the treatment of PV, SCD, and other hematologic disorders. We initiated RESTORE-PV, an open-label Phase 2 clinical trial of DISC-3405 in patients with PV, in the first half of 2025, with initial data expected in the second half of 2026. We also initiated a Phase 1b, open-label clinical trial of DISC-3405 in patients with SCD in October 2025, with initial data expected in the second half of 2026, and plan to explore the role of therapeutic iron restriction in other indications.

Our goal is to continue to build and advance a portfolio of product candidates that focus on fundamental biological pathways associated with the formation and function of red blood cells. Red blood cells have the essential role of carrying oxygen via hemoglobin to all tissues and organs in the body. The biological processes that are required to maintain normal levels of functional red blood cells are complex, and a variety of congenital and acquired diseases occur due to imbalances or deficiencies in red blood cell formation and function. Two key components needed to support the formation and function of red blood cells are heme and iron. Heme is an essential part of red blood cells, and when complexed into the hemoglobin protein, it performs the vital function of transporting oxygen throughout the body. Iron is a key component of heme, and therefore both iron and heme are required for erythropoiesis, the biological process by which precursor cells in the bone marrow mature to become red blood cells. Based on results in animal models and preclinical and clinical data, we believe that our product candidate portfolio, by targeting fundamental pathways in red blood cell biology, has the potential to address a range of hematologic diseases in which modification of iron and heme plays a critical function.

We are focused on therapeutic approaches that modulate heme and iron to address diseases of heme biosynthesis and red blood cell production, and we target therapeutic mechanisms that have been validated in humans, through evidence from either human genetics or third-party clinical trials. For example, our lead program, bitopertin, has been evaluated in over 4,000 individuals and demonstrated suppression of heme biosynthesis in multiple clinical trials conducted by Roche. The targets of our iron homeostasis portfolio, HJV and TMPRSS6, have both been genetically validated in humans and shown to have a role in the regulation of hepcidin and iron homeostasis. For example, individuals with inherited loss of the HJV gene exhibit low levels of hepcidin and individuals with inherited loss of the TMPRSS6 gene exhibit elevated levels of hepcidin.

By focusing on fundamental red blood cell biology that is validated in humans, we believe that our product candidates are more likely to exhibit well-defined biological effects in clinical trials and have the potential for broad applicability across a wide range of hematologic diseases. Our current pipeline is focused on the following three approaches:
• Modulating the heme biosynthesis pathway, which is anticipated to be useful in diseases caused by excesses in toxic heme pathway metabolites, e.g., EPs;

• Increasing iron availability to red blood cell precursors, which is anticipated to have direct effects on increasing red blood cell production to correct anemia in diseases of iron restriction, e.g., anemia associated with inflammatory diseases; and
• Decreasing iron availability, which is anticipated to lower red blood cell production in diseases of excessive red cell production, e.g., PV.

We are building an innovative pipeline of product candidates that aim to modify fundamental biological pathways associated with the formation and function of red blood cells. We have obtained exclusive, worldwide licenses for the development and commercialization of bitopertin, DISC-0974, and DISC-0998, and exclusive rights for DISC-3405 and related antibodies in all territories outside of Greater China and Southeast Asia.

headings: Risks Related to Our Limited Operating History, Financial Position and Capital Requirements
Our limited operating history may make it difficult for you to evaluate the success of our business to date and to assess our future viability.
We have incurred significant net losses since our inception and anticipate that we will continue to incur losses for the foreseeable future.
We have no products approved for commercial sale and have not generated any revenue from product sales.
Our existing and any future indebtedness could adversely affect our ability to operate our business.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our technologies or product candidates.
Risks Related to the Discovery and Development of Our Product Candidates
Clinical development involves a lengthy and expensive process, with an uncertain outcome.
We may incur additional costs or experience delays in initiating or completing, or ultimately be unable to complete, the development and commercialization of our product candidates.
If we experience delays or difficulties in the enrollment of patients in clinical trials, our receipt of necessary regulatory approvals could be delayed or prevented.
paragraphs: Set forth below are the risks that we believe are material to our investors and they should be carefully considered. If any of the following risks and uncertainties actually occurs, our business, prospects, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. The risks described below are not intended to be exhaustive and other factors not presently known to us or that we currently believe are immaterial may affect our business, prospects, financial condition and results of operations if they occur. This section contains forward-looking statements. You should refer to the explanation of the qualifications and limitations on forward-looking statements beginning on page ii of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We commenced operations in 2017 and are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with a limited operating history. Biopharmaceutical product development is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk. Since our inception in October 2017, we have devoted substantially all of our efforts to organizing and staffing our company, business planning, capital raising, establishing and maintaining our intellectual property portfolio, building our pipeline of product candidates, conducting drug discovery activities, undertaking preclinical studies, conducting clinical trials, preparing for the potential commercialization of bitopertin, if approved, and providing general and administrative support for these operations. We have not yet demonstrated our ability to successfully develop any product candidate, obtain regulatory approvals, manufacture a commercial-scale product or arrange for a third party to do so on our behalf, or conduct sales and marketing activities necessary for successful product commercialization. Consequently, any predictions you make about our future success or viability may not be as accurate as they could be if we had a longer operating history or a history of successfully developing and commercializing products.

In addition, as our business grows, we may encounter unforeseen expenses, difficulties, complications, delays and other known and unknown factors. We will need to transition at some point from a company with a research and development focus to a company capable of supporting commercial activities. We may not be successful in such a transition.

Our net losses were $212.2 million, $109.4 million and $76.4 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. We had an accumulated deficit of $510.2 million as of December 31, 2025. Substantially all of our net losses have resulted from costs incurred in connection with our research and development programs and from selling, general and administrative costs associated with our operations. We expect our research and development expenses to continue to increase significantly in connection with the commencement and continuation of clinical trials of our product candidates. In addition, if we obtain regulatory approval for our product candidates, we will incur significant sales, marketing and manufacturing expenses. We also will continue to incur additional costs associated with operating as a public company and expect to continue to incur significant and increasing operating losses over the next several years and for the foreseeable future. Because of the numerous risks and uncertainties associated with developing pharmaceutical products, we are unable to predict the extent of any future losses or when we will become profitable, if at all. Even if we do become profitable, we may not be able to sustain or increase our profitability on a quarterly or annual basis.

The amount of our future losses is uncertain and our quarterly and annual operating results may fluctuate significantly in the future due to a variety of factors, many of which are outside of our control and may be difficult to predict, including the following:

• the timing and success or failure of preclinical studies and clinical trials for our product candidates or competing product candidates, or any other change in the competitive landscape of our industry, including consolidation among our competitors or partners;

In October 2025 we completed an underwritten offering of shares of our common stock and pre-funded warrants for net proceeds of $211.0 million, after deducting offering expenses. As of December 31, 2025, we had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $791.2 million. We believe that our cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, will be sufficient to fund our current operating and capital expenditure plans and our debt service obligations into 2029, without taking into account any potential net cash inflows from bitopertin or any other marketed product, if approved during such period. We have based these estimates on assumptions that may prove to be wrong, and we could exhaust our available capital resources sooner than we expect. See "Liquidity and Capital Resources" for additional details.

If our development efforts are successful and result in commercialization of one or more product candidates or if we enter into collaboration or license agreements with third parties, we may generate revenue in the future from product sales, payments from such collaboration or license agreements or a combination thereof.
Research and development expenses consist primarily of costs incurred in connection with the research and development of our product candidates. These expenses include:
• employee-related expenses, including salaries, benefits, and stock-based compensation expense, for personnel engaged in research and development functions;

• expenses incurred in connection with our research and development activities, including under agreements with third parties such as consultants, contractors and contract research organizations, or CROs;

• costs related to contract development and manufacturing organizations, or CDMOs, that are primarily engaged to provide drug substance and product for our preclinical studies, clinical trials and research and development programs, as well as investigative sites and consultants that conduct our clinical trials, preclinical studies and other scientific development services;

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段生技藥品公司，專注於發現、開發及商業化用以治療罹患嚴重血液疾病患者的創新療法。本公司已組建了一組臨牀及臨牀前的產品候選藥物，旨在改變與紅血球形成及功能相關的基本生物途徑，特別是血紅素合成及鐵質平衡。本公司目前的產品開發管道包括用以治療紅血球生成性porphyrias（EPs），包括紅血球生成性原卟啉症（EPP）及X-linked原卟啉症（XLP）的bitopertin；用以治療骨髓纖維化性貧血（MF）及發炎性腸道疾病（IBD）性貧血的DISC-0974；以及用以治療真性紅血球增多症（PV）、鐮刀型細胞貧血症（SCD）及其他血液疾病的DISC-3405。此外，本公司臨牀前的開發計畫包括用以治療與發炎性疾病相關貧血的DISC-0998。本公司產品候選藥物的開發方法依賴已被人類驗證的分子機制。本公司認為，若這些產品候選藥物獲得核准，將有潛力改善罹患血液疾病的患者的生存品質。

Bitopertin為本公司在血紅素合成調節領域的領導產品候選藥物。Bitopertin先前由F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd及Hoffmann-La Roche Inc（合稱為Roche）在超過4,000名受試者中進行過一項全面臨牀計畫，顯示Bitopertin作為甘胺酸運輸體1（GlyT1）抑制劑的活性及其對血紅素合成的影響。本公司目前首先開發Bitopertin用以治療EPs，包括EPP及XLP，這些疾病屬於一組嚴重疾病，稱為porphyrias，是由血紅素合成途徑缺陷所導致，造成有毒代謝物（稱為卟啉）累積，進而導致皮膚對陽光及某些類型的人造光產生過敏反應。

本公司已完成Bitopertin的兩項二期臨牀試驗：BEACON為一項開放標籤、平行劑量的臨牀試驗，於澳洲的試驗點進行，用以評估EPP及XLP患者的治療效果；AURORA為一項隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照的臨牀試驗，於美國的試驗點進行，用以評估EPP患者的治療效果。在這兩項試驗中，Bitopertin顯著降低有毒代謝物，即原卟啉IX（PPIX），並與改善陽光曝曬時間及生活品質的指標相關。此外，Bitopertin通常耐受性良好。所有參與AURORA及BEACON試驗的受試者均有資格參與HELIOS，一項持續進行的開放標籤、長期延續試驗，用以評估Bitopertin在EPP及XLP患者的治療效果。HELIOS的中期數據於2025年6月發表，顯示長期使用Bitopertin與PPIX的持續降低相關，並改善生活品質及肝臟生物指標。在2024年9月的二期結束會議中，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）同意PPIX的降低可作為支持Bitopertin在EPP及XLP加速核准的替代終點。在2024年12月的Type C會議中，本公司與FDA達成共識，設計APOLLO試驗，一項三期、隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照的臨牀試驗，用以評估Bitopertin在EPP及XLP患者的治療效果，若在加速核准的情況下，此試驗將作為上市後確認試驗。本公司於2025年5月啟動APOLLO試驗，並於2025年9月提交美國加速核准的新藥申請（NDA），基於現有數據。2025年10月，本公司獲頒FDA的委員國家優先級券（CNPV），用以加速Bitopertin在EPP及XLP的開發與審查。CNPV計畫於2025年6月宣佈，旨在加速某些與美國國家健康優先事項相符的藥物的開發與審查。FDA於2025年11月接受本公司NDA進行審查，並於2026年2月發出完整回應信（CRL）。雖然FDA同意AURORA及BEACON的臨牀數據顯示Bitopertin顯著降低全血無金屬PPIX，但FDA認為試驗未顯示PPIX百分比變化與試驗中陽光曝曬相關終點的關聯性。因此，FDA認為Bitopertin對PPIX的影響是否合理預測臨牀效益仍存在不確定性，儘管強大的機制及生物學合理性支持使用PPIX生物指標於原卟啉症的治療。FDA表示APOLLO試驗的結果可能作為支持傳統核准的證據，本公司計畫請求與FDA進行Type A會議審查我們的策略。我們預期於2026年第四季報告APOLLO的初步數據，之後計畫提交對CRL的回應。
APOLLO臨牀試驗也預期作為Bitopertin在EPP及XLP於美國以外的潛在市場申請的註冊試驗。本公司持續評估Bitopertin在其他適應症的潛在試驗。

DISC-0974 是本公司在鐵離子平衡零組件中的領先產品候選藥物，並自 AbbVie Deutschland GmbH & Co. KG，或 AbbVie 獲得授權。DISC-0974 設計用以抑制肝臟激素（hepcidin）的產生並增加血液中的鐵離子濃度。本公司於 2022 年 6 月在美國完成針對健康志工的 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，試驗結果顯示可接受的耐受性與目標作用證據、鐵離子移動及紅血球生成增加。本公司於 2022 年 6 月啟動針對 MF 疾病相關貧血患者的 Phase 1b/2 臨牀試驗，此臨牀試驗的 Phase 1b 部分結果顯示肝臟激素濃度顯著且持續下降，鐵離子濃度增加，並在不同患者類型中顯示強烈的血液學反應，且具有可接受的耐受性。本公司於 2024 年 12 月啟動 RALLY-MF，為此臨牀試驗的開放標籤 Phase 2 部分，並於 2025 年 12 月報告此 Phase 2 試驗的初步數據，結果顯示在所有患者亞組中，不論基線輸血狀態如何，且與同時使用 Janus Kinase，或 JAK，抑制劑治療無關，均顯示顯著的整體貧血反應。此試驗的總體數據預計於 2026 年第二季公佈，若結果為正，預期將支持與監管機構討論 DISC-0974 在 MF 疾病相關貧血的潛在監管途徑。本公司於 2026 年第一季啟動針對 IBD 並有貧血患者的 DISC-0974 Phase 2 臨牀試驗，並計畫在其他有慢性疾病相關貧血的患者羣體中進行探索性研究。本公司也正在開發一種預臨牀用的抗 hemojuvelin，或 HJV，單株抗體，DISC-0998，此藥物也針對肝臟激素抑制，並自 AbbVie 獲得授權。DISC-0998 設計用以增加血液中的鐵離子濃度，與 DISC-0974 相較，其血液中半衰期較長。本公司認為此特性可能在某些與發炎性疾病相關貧血的患者子羣中具有優勢。

此外，本公司正在開發 DISC-3405，一種針對 Transmembrane Serine Protease 6，或 TMPRSS6 的單株抗體，並自 Mabwell Therapeutics, Inc.，或 Mabwell 獲得授權。DISC-3405 屬於本公司鐵離子平衡零組件，設計用以誘導肝臟激素（hepcidin）產生並降低血液中的鐵離子濃度。本公司於 2023 年 10 月啟動針對健康成人志工的 DISC-3405 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，並於 2024 年 6 月展示此臨牀試驗單劑遞增（single-ascending dose，或 SAD）部分的中期數據。本公司於 2024 年 12 月展示此臨牀試驗多劑遞增（multiple ascending dose，或 MAD）部分的數據，並於 2025 年 6 月展示來自 SAD 與 MAD 部分的更新數據，結果顯示可接受的耐受性與目標作用證據，包括劑量相關的血液中肝臟激素濃度增加與對應的血液中鐵離子濃度下降，於所有劑量層次均觀察到此現象。本公司正在開發 DISC-3405 用以治療 PV、SCD 以及其他血液疾病。本公司於 2025 年第一季啟動 RESTORE-PV，為針對 PV 患者的開放標籤 Phase 2 臨牀試驗，預計於 2026 年第二季公佈初步數據。本公司也於 2025 年 10 月啟動針對 SCD 患者的 DISC-3405 Phase 1b，開放標籤臨牀試驗，預計於 2026 年第二季公佈初步數據，並計畫探索治療性鐵離子限制在其他適應症中的角色。

本公司目標為持續建立並推進一組專注於紅血球形成與功能相關基本生物途徑的產品候選藥物。紅血球具有將氧氣透過血紅蛋白運送到全身組織與器官的關鍵功能。維持正常功能紅血球水平所需的生物過程相當複雜，而許多先天與後天疾病皆因紅血球形成與功能的不平衡或缺乏而產生。支持紅血球形成與功能的兩個關鍵零組件為血紅素（heme）與鐵離子。血紅素是紅血球的重要組成部分，當與血紅蛋白蛋白結合時，便能執行將氧氣運送到全身的關鍵功能。鐵離子是血紅素的關鍵組成部分，因此鐵離子與血紅素皆為紅血球生成（erythropoiesis），即骨髓中前驅細胞成熟為紅血球的生物過程所必需。根據動物模型與預臨牀及臨牀數據結果，本公司相信，透過針對紅血球生物學的基本途徑，本公司產品候選藥物有潛力治療那些鐵離子與血紅素改變在其中扮演關鍵角色的血液疾病。

本公司專注於調節血紅素與鐵離子的治療方法，以解決血紅素合成疾病與紅血球生成疾病，並針對已在人類中驗證的治療機制進行開發，這些機制的證據來自人類遺傳學或第三方臨牀試驗。例如，本公司領先計畫 bitopertin 已在超過 4,000 名個體中進行評估，並在 Roche 進行的多項臨牀試驗中顯示抑制血紅素合成。本公司鐵離子平衡零組件的目標 HJV 與 TMPRSS6，皆已在人類中透過遺傳學驗證，並顯示其在調節肝臟激素與鐵離子平衡中的作用。例如，具有遺傳性 HJV 基因缺失的個體會顯示肝臟激素濃度偏低，而具有遺傳性 TMPRSS6 基因缺失的個體則會顯示肝臟激素濃度偏高。
透過聚焦於在人類中已驗證的基本紅血球生物學，我們認為我們的產品候選藥物在臨牀試驗中較可能表現出明確的生物學效果，並具有在廣泛的血液疾病中應用的潛力。我們目前的產品開發路線圖聚焦於以下三個方向：
• 調節血紅素合成路徑，預期對由過量有毒血紅素路徑代謝物所引起的疾病有幫助，例如 EPs；
• 增加鐵元素對紅血球前驅細胞的可得性，預期對增加紅血球生成以矯正鐵缺乏性貧血有直接效果，例如與發炎性疾病相關的貧血；以及
• 減少鐵元素的可得性，預期會降低紅血球生成，在過度紅血球生成的疾病中，例如 PV。
我們正在建立一個創新產品候選藥物的開發路線圖，目標是修改與紅血球形成與功能相關的基本生物學路徑。我們已取得 bitopertin、DISC-0974 和 DISC-0998 的獨家、全球開發與商業化許可，並取得 DISC-3405 及相關單株抗體在大中華地區與東南亞以外所有地區的獨家權利。
下圖反映我們臨牀階段產品候選藥物 bitopertin、DISC-0974 和 DISC-3405 以及相關臨牀試驗，以及我們的前期臨牀產品候選藥物 DISC-0998 的現狀。圖中顯示的時間線反映我們目前的預期與信念，基於我們的內部計畫與至今的監管互動。

Bitopertin 為我們血紅素合成調節組合之主要產品候選藥物。Bitopertin 曾由 F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd 及 Hoffmann-La Roche Inc.，或合稱 Roche，在其他適應症中進行過一項全面臨牀計畫，參與人數超過 4,000 人，顯示 bitopertin 為一甘胺酸運輸子 1，或 GlyT1，抑制劑，並對血紅素合成產生影響。我們目前首先開發 bitopertin 用以治療 EPs，包括 EPP 及 XLP，這些為一組嚴重疾病，稱為卟啉症，由血紅素合成途徑缺陷所導致，造成有毒代謝物，稱為卟啉，累積，導致皮膚對陽光及某些類型人工光源產生過敏反應。

我們已完成 bitopertin 的第二階段臨牀試驗兩項：BEACON，為一項開放標籤、平行劑量的臨牀試驗，於澳洲的試驗場地進行，針對 EPP 和 XLP 患者；以及 AURORA，為一項隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照的臨牀試驗，於美國的試驗場地進行，針對 EPP 患者。在這兩項試驗中，bitopertin 明顯降低有毒代謝物，即原卟啉 IX，或 PPIX，並與改善陽光曝曬時間和生活品質的指標有關。此外，bitopertin 通常耐受性良好。所有參與 AURORA 和 BEACON 的參與者均有資格參與 HELIOS，為一項持續進行的開放標籤、長期延續研究，針對 EPP 和 XLP 患者。HELIOS 的中期資料於 2025 年 6 月發表，顯示長期使用 bitopertin 會與 PPIX 的持續降低有關，同時也改善生活品質和肝臟生物指標。在 2024 年 9 月的第二階段結案會議中，美國食品藥物管理局，或 FDA，同意 PPIX 減少的潛力可用作替代終點，以支持 bitopertin 在 EPP 和 XLP 的加速批准。在 2024 年 12 月的 Type C 會議中，我們與 FDA 針對 APOLLO 的設計達成共識，APOLLO 為一項第三階段、隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照的臨牀試驗，針對 EPP 和 XLP 患者，在加速批准的情況下，將作為上市後確認試驗。我們於 2025 年 5 月啟動 APOLLO 試驗，並於 2025 年 9 月提交新藥申請，或 NDA，以支持 bitopertin 在 EPP 和 XLP 的加速批准。2025 年 10 月，我們獲得了 FDA 發放的委員會國家優先級憑證，或 CNPV，針對 bitopertin 在 EPP 和 XLP 的應用。CNPV 計畫於 2025 年 6 月宣佈，旨在加速符合美國國家健康優先級的某些藥物的開發與審查。FDA 於 2025 年 11 月接受我們的 NDA 進行審查，並於 2026 年 2 月發出完整回應信，或 CRL。儘管 FDA 同意 AURORA 和 BEACON 的臨牀資料提供了足夠證據顯示 bitopertin 明顯降低全血無金屬 PPIX，但 FDA 結論認為這些試驗未顯示 PPIX 百分比變化與陽光曝曬基準端點之間的關聯。因此，FDA 判斷 bitopertin 對 PPIX 的影響是否能合理預測臨牀效益存在不確定性，儘管強大的機制和生物學合理性支持使用 PPIX 生物指標於原卟啉症。FDA 指出 APOLLO 試驗的結果可能作為支持傳統批准的證據，我們計畫請求 Type A 會議與 FDA 討論我們的策略。我們預計於 2026 年第四季報告 APOLLO 的初步資料，之後計畫提交對 CRL 的回應。
我們的 APOLLO 臨牀試驗也預期作為未來在美國以外地區申請 bitopertin 在 EPP 和 XLP 的市場許可的註冊試驗。我們持續評估 bitopertin 在其他適應症的潛在試驗。

DISC-0974 是我們鐵調節組閤中的領先產品候選藥物，並從 AbbVie Deutschland GmbH & Co. KG，或 AbbVie 授予許可。DISC-0974 設計用以抑制肝細胞激素的產生並增加血清鐵水平。我們於 2022 年 6 月在美國完成健康志願者中的第一階段臨牀試驗，結果顯示可接受的耐受性與目標作用、鐵離子移動和紅血球生成的證據。我們於 2022 年 6 月啟動針對 MF 疾病相關貧血患者的 Phase 1b/2 臨牀試驗，此試驗的第一階段結果顯示肝細胞激素水平顯著且持續降低，鐵水平增加，並在不同患者類型中顯示強烈的血液學反應，且耐受性可接受。我們於 2024 年 12 月啟動 RALLY-MF，為此臨牀試驗的開放標籤第二階段部分，並於 2025 年 12 月報告此第二階段試驗的初步資料，結果顯示在所有患者亞組中均有顯著的整體貧血反應，不論基線輸血狀態，且與同時使用 Janus Kinase，或 JAK，抑制劑治療無關。此試驗的初步資料預計於 2026 年第二季公佈，若結果正面，預期將支持與監管機構討論 DISC-0974 在 MF 相關貧血的潛在監管路徑。我們於 2026 年第一季啟動 DISC-0974 在 IBD 和貧血患者的第二階段臨牀試驗，並計畫在其他慢性疾病相關貧血患者羣體中進行探索性研究。我們也在開發一種預臨牀抗 hemojuvelin，或 HJV，單株抗體，DISC-0998，該藥物也針對肝細胞激素抑制，並從 AbbVie 授予許可。DISC-0998 設計用以增加血清鐵水平，其血清半衰期較 DISC-0974 更長。我們認為此特性可能在某些與炎症疾病相關貧血的患者子羣中具有優勢。

此外，我們正在開發 DISC-3405，一種針對 Transmembrane Serine Protease 6，或 TMPRSS6 的單株抗體，並從 Mabwell Therapeutics, Inc.，或 Mabwell 授予許可。DISC-3405 是我們鐵調節組合的一部分，設計用以誘導肝細胞激素產生並降低血清鐵水平。我們於 2023 年 10 月在健康成人志願者中啟動 DISC-3405 的第一階段臨牀試驗，並於 2024 年 6 月發表此臨牀試驗單劑遞增，或 SAD，部分的中期資料。我們於 2024 年 12 月發表此臨牀試驗多劑遞增，或 MAD，部分的資料，並於 2025 年 6 月發表更新的 SAD 和 MAD 部分資料，結果顯示可接受的耐受性與目標作用證據，包括劑量相關的血清肝細胞激素增加和對應的血清鐵減少，於所有劑量層次均顯示此現象。我們正在開發 DISC-3405 用於治療 PV、SCD 和其他血液疾病。我們於 2025 年第一季啟動 RESTORE-PV，為一項開放標籤第二階段臨牀試驗，針對 PV 患者，預計於 2026 年第二季公佈初步資料。我們也於 2025 年 10 月啟動 DISC-3405 在 SCD 患者的 Phase 1b、開放標籤臨牀試驗，預計於 2026 年第二季公佈初步資料，並計畫探索治療性鐵限制在其他適應症中的角色。

2025 年 10 月，我們完成了一項經承銷的普通股發行及預資助的認購權證發行，淨資金為 211.0 百萬美元，扣除發行費用後。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們持有現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券共 791.2 百萬美元。我們認為，我們的現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券，將足以支應我們目前的營運及資本支出計畫，以及債務償還義務，至 2029 年為止，不考慮任何潛在的比特普瑞汀或任何其他上市產品的淨現金流入，若在該期間內獲得核准。我們這些估計是基於可能錯誤的假設，我們可能比預期更快耗盡可用的資金。請參閱「流動性及資本資源」以取得更多細節。
自我們成立以來，我們尚未產生任何收入，且在可預見的未來，我們不預期會因產品銷售而產生任何收入，若有的話。如果我們的開發工作成功，並導致一個或多個產品候選藥物的商業化，或我們與第三方簽訂合作或授權協議，我們未來可能因產品銷售、合作或授權協議的付款，或兩者結合而產生收入。
研究與開發費用主要為與我們產品候選藥物的研究與開發相關的支出。這些費用包括：
• 與從事研究與開發功能的員工相關的支出，包括薪資、福利及股票基於薪酬費用；
• 與我們研究與開發活動相關的支出，包括與第三方簽訂的協議下的費用，例如顧問、承包商及合同研究組織，或 CROs；
• 與合同開發與製造組織，或 CDMOs，相關的成本，這些組織主要用於為我們的動物實驗、臨牀試驗及研究與開發計畫提供藥物原料及產品，以及進行我們臨牀試驗、動物實驗及其他科學開發服務的試驗場地及顧問。

headings: 與本公司有限經營歷史、財務狀況及資金需求相關之風險
本公司有限之經營歷史可能使您難以評估本公司迄今之業務成效，並難以評估本公司未來之生存能力。
自本公司成立以來，我們已產生重大淨虧損，並預期在可預見之未來，我們將持續產生虧損。
本公司目前尚無已核准上市之產品，且尚未從產品銷售中產生任何營業收入。
本公司現有及未來任何負債可能對本公司經營業務之能力產生不利影響。
籌措額外資金可能導致股東持股稀釋，限制本公司之營運活動，或要求本公司放棄對我們之智慧財產權或產品候選藥物之權利。
與本公司產品候選藥物之發現及開發相關之風險
臨牀開發涉及漫長且昂貴的過程，且結果具有不確定性。
本公司可能產生額外成本或遭遇延宕，導致無法啟動或完成，或最終無法完成產品候選品的開發與商業化。
若本公司在臨牀試驗中遭遇患者招募延宕或困難，將可能導致取得必要監管核准的時間延後或無法取得。
paragraphs: 下列為我們認為對投資人具重大影響之風險，請謹慎考量。若任何下列風險與不確定性實際發生，將可能對我們之業務、前景、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利之影響。下列所描述之風險並非完整列出，其他未為我們所知或目前認為不具重大影響之因素，若發生，亦可能對我們之業務、前景、財務狀況及營運成果造成影響。本節包含前瞻性陳述。請參閱本年度報告表10-K第ii頁開始之前瞻性陳述之說明與限制事項。

我們於2017年開始營運，為一家臨牀階段生技藥品公司，具有有限之營運歷史。生技藥品產品之開發為極具風險之高度投機性活動。自2017年10月成立以來，我們已投入大部分之努力於組織與僱用員工、業務規劃、資金籌措、建立與維護智慧財產權組合、建立產品候選藥物之產品線、進行藥物發現活動、進行非臨牀研究、進行臨牀試驗、準備bitopertin若獲批准之商業化潛力，以及提供一般及行政支援以支持這些營運。我們尚未證明我們能成功開發任何產品候選藥物、取得監管核准、製造商業規模之產品或委請第三方代為執行，或進行銷售與行銷活動以實現產品之商業化。因此，您對我們未來成功或存續之預測可能不如我們有更長之營運歷史或成功開發與商業化產品之歷史為準。
此外，隨著我們業務成長，我們可能面臨未預見之費用、困難、複雜性、延宕及其他已知與未知之因素。我們將在某個時點必須從以研究與開發為重點之公司轉型為能支持商業活動之公司。我們可能無法成功進行此轉型。

我們之淨虧損為212.2 百萬美元、109.4 百萬美元及76.4 百萬美元，分別為2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31年之財務年度。截至2025年12月31日，我們之累積虧損為510.2 百萬美元。我們之淨虧損幾乎全部來自與我們研究與開發計畫相關之費用，以及與我們營運相關之銷售、一般及行政費用。我們預期與我們產品候選藥物之臨牀試驗之啟動與持續進行相關之研究與開發費用將持續顯著增加。此外，若我們取得產品候選藥物之監管核准，我們將產生顯著之銷售、行銷與製造費用。我們亦將持續產生與作為上市公司營運相關之額外費用，並預期在未來數年及可預見之未來持續產生顯著且增加之營運虧損。由於開發藥品產品所涉及之多項風險與不確定性，我們無法預測未來虧損之範圍或我們何時能實現盈利（若有可能）。即使我們實現盈利，我們可能無法維持或提高季度或年度之盈利表現。
我們未來虧損之金額無法預測，且我們之季度與年度營運結果可能因多種因素而大幅波動，許多因素為我們所無法控制且難以預測，包括以下各項：
• 非臨牀研究與臨牀試驗之時程及成功或失敗，以及我們產品候選藥物或競爭產品候選藥物之任何變動，或任何其他產業競爭環境之變動，包括我們競爭對手或合作夥伴之合併。
